decisions.reason: Operator training is cheap to run, draws on the firm's established training and service capabilities, and supports machine sales and customer retention, so withdrawing it makes little sense.
A fourth rotary axis is a standard, low-cost accessory that extends the firm's core milling machines and generates add-on sales, so it is likely to stay in the range.

Hybrid additive post-processing is distant from the core business and was only mentioned on the website, which makes it the most vulnerable product, but its link to digital fabrication and the firm's future-oriented strategy argues for keeping it a while longer.
The high-speed CNC milling machine line is the firm's core business, has several models and its own page, and fits a growing industry, so dropping it is very unlikely.
Automatic tool changing is an integral productivity feature for the firm's machines and builds directly on its established offer, so it will very likely be kept.
